chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
title: Dakota Staton at the 1960 Newport and Atlantic City festivals
summary: Newport draws a rowdy non-jazz crowd, and in Atlantic City he hangs out with Oscar Peterson.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Meantime, I began to get calls from other people. It was

during this time when I got a call from Dakota Staton. And I went to New York, rehearsed with her, and then we... I think we worked maybe a club or so, but the big thing that I remember about her (I think it was 1960) was the Newport Jazz Festival. It was the year they had a big riot up there. Well, it wasn't a riot, but people just went crazy, because so many people that came to the Festival that really didn't care anything about Jazz, but the idea of people coming together was something like the thing they had at Woodstock was it...?
Oh, Woodstock was a big thing later on.
They had a big thing later on...

Yeah, a Rock kind of thing. Well, they had a lot of people like that up there that came up... I remember people walking through the streets with whole bottles of whiskey, fifths and what have you in their hand, just drinking out of the bottle. Of course, there was people in bathing suits, and hollering and screaming like they were in some little town in Texas somewhere. And these very seemed like conservative people looking at them, like, in wonder, like "What the hell is going on in our town?" Anyway, that was quite an experience there, the Newport Jazz Festival. I think it was

1960...
We left there and went to Atlantic City, and we played the Atlantic City Jazz Festival, which was quite an experience. I got to hang out with Oscar Peterson and the trio, and a lot of other people. We worked Atlantic City, and leaving there... I think we did a club there after the Festival. Our next engagement was in Chicago at the Show Lounge out there on the... Oh, I can't remember the name off it. [PROBABLY THE ROBERTS SHOW LOUNGE ON 63rd STREET] It was a big club. We did two weeks there, I believe.
